verifyByViolating.liveBugCaughtAndFixed: The first live run exposed a real defect this fixture-only unit-testing had not caught: node-postgres returns a timestamptz column as a JS Date object, and stampCurrencyNote's template-literal interpolation of a raw Date renders via Date.prototype.toString() -- a locale/timezone-shifted string (e.g. 'Wed Sep 02 2026 23:38:06 GMT-0500...' for a UTC 2026-09-03T04:38:06.918Z value), not the deterministic UTC instant. Fixed by normalizing ingested_at to an ISO string at loadResidueWithRealZoning's DB-read boundary (Date instanceof check), so every downstream consumer sees the same representation regardless of environment timezone. Re-ran the live probe after the fix and confirmed clean ISO strings throughout. A regression test (a real Date instance, not a string fixture) was added so this class of bug cannot silently return.
